We present (i) \emph{self-informed sampling (SIFS)}, a data-efficient expert-sampling strategy that uses a learned time-to-go to query the expert only where the policy deviates from time-optimal behavior, (ii) a complete training and control architecture that jointly addresses dataset correlation, suboptimal expert labels, covariate shift, constraint satisfaction and model mismatch, and (iii) real-world validation on a Furuta pendulum. SIFS matches standard dataset aggregation performance in roughly one-third of the training time and with less than half the training data. The resulting controller matches the region of attraction of the expert TOMPC while raising the control frequency from 1.4~Hz to 1~kHz. On hardware, the controller swings up and stabilizes the pendulum along trajectories closely matching the expert TOMPC solution.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: CT-RespGeomLib: Deterministic reconstruction of CT airway masks into editable,port-matched lumen geometry
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: Patient-specific airway modelling requires geometrically consistent lumen surfaces with identifiable boundaries and support for controlled anatomical modifications. We present CT-RespGeomLib, a deterministic framework that converts CT airway masks into two complementary representations: an editable assembly of semantically labelled pipe and junction blocks connected through canonical shared ports, and a fused lumen surface reconstructed from tapered implicit primitives with validated port-to-boundary loop correspondence. The parametric representation further enables localised modelling of airway stenosis and dilation without re-segmentation. Evaluated on 42 reference airway masks from ATM22 (15 cases) and AeroPath (27 cases), the framework produced 37 topologically accepted reconstructions, with a median port-to-loop distance of 0.123 mm across 2174 matched ports. Reconstructed and reference equivalent radii showed strong agreement ($R^2 = 0.976$), with a mean bias of -0.414 mm arising primarily from the circular, inscribed-radius representation. Controlled pathology modelling generated 40 variants across five patient-specific geometries, including 25-75% stenosis and 50% dilation at tracheal and main-bronchus locations. Prescribed radius changes were reproduced with a mean absolute ratio error of 0.0056, while the median 95th-percentile deviation outside the modified region was 0.111 mm. Downstream applicability was demonstrated through volume meshing and an OpenFOAM simulation with individually prescribed model-based resistance conditions at 62 outlets. Although additional surface preparation may be required for numerical meshing, CT-RespGeomLib provides a reproducible framework for CT-derived airway reconstruction, quantitative boundary validation and controlled geometric pathology modelling.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Survivability Guarantees for Delayed Serial Supply Chains under Demand Shocks
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: When demand exceeds the maximum production capacity of a supply chain, it can be satisfied only for a finite time, determined by the inventory stored along the chain. Existing control methods ensure indefinite constraint satisfaction under bounded demand, but provide no guarantees on how long a supply chain can withstand a shock in which demand goes beyond production capacity. We address this gap for a serial supply chain with transportation delays and flow constraints. Under a specified flow policy, we derive necessary and sufficient conditions on the inventory distribution that guarantee a prescribed lower bound on the exit time from the set where demand is served. We use these conditions to compute inventory targets that minimize holding costs via a quadratic program. Then, we propose a two-mode controller that builds reserves under ordinary demand and depletes them during the shock. Simulations illustrate this approach.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: A Modulation Strategy for Bidirectional Integrated Onboard and Wireless EV Charging
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: Integrated electric vehicle chargers reduce cost by sharing power conversion hardware between the onboard charger (OBC) and the wireless charger (WC). A previously proposed dual active bridge (DAB)-based OBC/WC shares the rectification stage between the OBC and WC; however, the modulation required to realize its wireless operation has not yet been reported. This paper details a modulation strategy that enables the operation of the integrated OBC/WC topology. Differential-mode operation is used for the OBC, and common-mode operation is used for the WC. In OBC mode, the shared full-bridge produces differential-mode voltage for wired power transfer while ideally generating zero common-mode voltage on the wireless charging path. In WC mode, the same full-bridge produces common-mode voltage for wireless power transfer while ideally generating zero differential-mode voltage on the onboard charging path. The method preserves conventional DAB phase-shift power control and enables bidirectional power transfer in wired and wireless charging modes without additional contactors. Design considerations for the OBC transformer and WC coils are derived based on the resulting square-wave voltage amplitudes. Offline PLECS simulations demonstrate power tracking and decoupled charger operation at $\pm$7.4 kW. Hardware-in-the-loop simulations using a PLECS RT Box and an external Texas Instruments microcontroller further validate the proposed modulation method.
Systems and Control (EESS).comment: 7 pages, 9 figures. Accepted version of a paper presented at the 2026 IEEE Energy Conversion Congress and Expo (ECCE), Vancouver, Canada

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Improved Single-Input Space Vector for DC-Biased Sinusoidal Current Control in Battery Cyclers
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: This paper presents improvements to the single-input space vector (SISV) concept for current control in a battery cycler based on a two-phase interleaved buck converter. The cycler is controlled to output a dc-biased sinusoidal current, enabling investigation of second-harmonic ripple effects on lithium-ion cell aging. A modified SISV generation scheme is introduced to track current references containing both dc and sinusoidal components, and an impedance-angle compensation method is proposed to decouple the d and q control axes without disturbing dc tracking. A dq phase-portrait visualization method is also introduced to evaluate transient performance for both SISV and proportional-integral-resonant (PIR) control methods. Simulation and experimental results validate dc-biased sinusoidal current tracking using PIR control and SISV control with different decoupling schemes. The phase-portrait framework allows for straightforward evaluation of transient performance for both SISV and PIR control methods and supports controller tuning to obtain desired trajectories. The results demonstrate the feasibility of SISV-based current control as an alternative to PIR control for battery-cycler applications. The proposed improvements support the development of battery cyclers capable of controlling both dc and sinusoidal current components.
Systems and Control (EESS).comment: 8 pages, 17 figures. Accepted version of a paper presented at the 2026 IEEE Energy Conversion Congress and Expo (ECCE), Vancouver, Canada

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Physics-informed structured learning of a class of recurrent neural networks with guaranteed properties
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: This paper proposes a physics-informed learning framework for a class of recurrent neural networks tailored to networked systems. The approach aims to learn control-oriented models that preserve the structural and stability properties of the plant. The learning algorithm is formulated as a convex optimisation problem, allowing the inclusion of linear matrix inequality constraints to enforce desired plant features. Furthermore, when the plant exhibits structural modularity, the resulting optimisation problem can be parallelised, requiring communication only among neighbouring subplants. Simulation results show the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: SAGAS: Semantic-Aware Graph-Assisted Stitching for Offline Temporal Logic Planning
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: Linear Temporal Logic (LTL) provides a rigorous framework for specifying long-horizon robotic tasks, yet existing approaches face a trade-off: model-based synthesis relies on accurate labeled transition systems, whereas learning-based methods often require online interaction, task-specific rewards, or specification-conditioned training. We study LTL-specified robotic planning and execution in an offline, model-free setting, where the agent is given only fixed, task-agnostic trajectory fragments, with no dynamics model, task demonstrations, or online data collection. To address this setting, we propose SAGAS, a framework that combines the compositionality of symbolic synthesis with the data-driven reachability structure learned from offline trajectories. SAGAS first learns a reusable latent reachability graph and a frozen goal-conditioned executor from fragmented offline data. For each new LTL formula, it performs task-time semantic graph augmentation to ground state-defined propositions on the learned graph and applies Büchi product search to synthesize a cost-aware accepting prefix--suffix waypoint plan executed by the frozen executor. This separation of learning and planning enables zero-shot generalization to unseen LTL formulas and new predicates supported by the offline data, without task-specific rewards, additional data collection, or policy retraining. Experiments on LTL task suites constructed from OGBench locomotion domains show that SAGAS achieves higher success rates and lower execution costs than baselines on diverse unseen tasks, with further evaluation in OGBench Scene demonstrating its applicability to robotic manipulation.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Mode-in-Variance Participation Factors under Stochastic Excitation
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: This paper investigates how the dynamic modes of a power system contribute to the stationary variance of its variables under continuous stochastic excitation. Using a modal decomposition of the covariance matrix, the variance of each state or algebraic variable can be resolved into components associated with individual modal responses and their interactions. These components are shown to correspond to within-mode variance and cross-modal covariance, respectively, and the corresponding normalized contributions are termed mode-in-variance participation factors (PFs). The proposed PFs can be used to identify modes governing the variability of important system quantities such as frequency and voltage, quantify the effect of modal interactions, and reveal control dynamics that can be targeted to reduce their stochastic variability. These capabilities are demonstrated through case studies based on the Kundur two-area and IEEE 39-bus systems.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: A New Analytical Method and Interpretation of Loss-of-Load Counts
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: This paper establishes the relationship between loss-of-load expectation (LOLE) and loss-of-load frequency (LOLF). We show why LOLE generally does not measure distinct-event frequency, mean event duration, or shortage magnitude. We identify conditions under which peak-based LOLE admits a frequency interpretation as the expected count of deficient daily peaks per horizon and distinguish this quantity from LOLF. We also derive an analytical formulation for frequency-and-duration indices that combines a convolution-derived generation probability-and-frequency model with chronological load changes. Under stationary generation, it uses the prescribed load profile directly, without constructing a separate load model or discretizing load magnitudes. Studies using generation and load data from the 24-bus IEEE RTS reveal different event frequencies and mean event durations at identical peak-based LOLE, motivating their separate assessment. Numerical comparisons demonstrate the accuracy advantage of the proposed analytical calculation over the conventional analytical implementations, quantifying the LOLF errors incurred by load discretization.
Systems and Control (EESS).comment: 5 pages, 3 figures, 1 table, submitted to IEEE PESGM

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Adjacent Heat Transfer Effects Can Bias Savings Estimates When Controlling Only Part of a Multi-Zone Building
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: Field demonstrations of advanced heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning control often operate a few thermal zones within a larger building and report savings for those zones alone. A recent theorem showed that this practice overestimates whole-building savings, because heat drawn from the neighboring zones is paid for by their equipment and is not counted. The error grows with the thermal conductance between the controlled and uncontrolled zones, with how much colder the controlled zones run over the test, and with the price of the heat their neighbors supply. For one controlled zone with one neighbor, a single thermal price, and slowly changing prices, the relative error reduces to the ratio of two conductances, a screening number that can be evaluated from the two conductances before a demonstration begins. This paper tests how far that reduction can be taken. A two-story house with one thermal zone per floor is simulated over a 90-day heating season in West Lafayette, Indiana, with receding-horizon model predictive control on the first floor and setpoint control on the second, under four combinations of electricity tariff (time-of-use or flat) and heating plant (heat pump or electric resistance). The exact correction from the theorem recovers the true savings in every case, and the full theorem, evaluated from the controlled zone's temperatures, the prices, and the building parameters, reproduces the measured relative error in every case. The conductance ratio bounds that error from above in all four cases, tightly under a flat tariff, within 3%, and loosely under a time-of-use tariff, where most of the controller's savings come from shifting load through the thermal mass rather than from lowering the temperature.
Systems and Control (EESS).comment: 10 pages. Accepted at the 2027 ASHRAE Winter Conference

Systems and Control (EESS).title: On the Nyquist Criterion and the Scaled Relative Graph for SISO systems: A Generalized Circle Criterion
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: Scaled Relative Graphs (SRGs) provide a novel graphical frequency-domain method for the analysis of nonlinear systems. However, existing SRG-based methods are limited to stable open-loop dynamics and can lead to false conclusions when applied to unstable Linear and Time-Invariant (LTI) components. In this paper, we identify the source of this pitfall and resolve it by introducing the extended SRG, which augments the SRG of an LTI system with the encirclement information of the Nyquist criterion. We show how the extended SRG can be used for stability and $H_\infty$-performance analysis of LTI systems and the computation of SRGs for unstable LTI systems. Building on these results, we derive graphical stability and incremental $L_2$-gain conditions for three canonical nonlinear feedback interconnections: the Lur'e system, the controlled Lur'e system, and an LTI plant with Lur'e controller. As a corollary, we derive a user-friendly generalized circle criterion that relates the $L_2$-gain directly to separation between the Nyquist curve and the critical disk from the classical circle criterion, requiring SRGs only for the proof, not its statement. The proposed approach is validated on several examples involving unstable LTI dynamics and nonlinearities, demonstrating applicability beyond the capabilities of existing SRG methods.
Systems and Control (EESS).comment: Revised version of the paper previously titled "Scaled Relative Graph Analysis of General Interconnections of SISO Nonlinear Systems"

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Quantum Network Flows That Solve Linear Equations
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: We develop a distributed quantum network flow for solving linear equations from locally stored row data. Local pumping enforces each node's equation constraint, while neighboring registers interact through swaps. The node marginals obey an exact, closed flow combining consensus with local constraint enforcement. For consistent equations, all node states converge exponentially to a common state supported on the solution space; a unique solution yields full-network convergence to the product solution state. For inconsistent equations of full column rank, scaled encoding and readout recover the least-squares solution through successive large-gain and small-scale limits. For consistent systems, the marginal convergence rate is nondecreasing and concave in the swap gain, approaching a graph-independent limit for fixed local dissipators. Its leading finite-gain correction couples graph topology and row placement through the Laplacian pseudoinverse, enabling semidefinite optimization of edge rates under a fixed total swap-rate budget. For invertible systems, a dissipative HHL-type construction using the same pumping law provides a comparison of solution-state encodings, decay rates, and row-update locality under squared-row-norm pumping. Numerical examples are provided to validate the presented results.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: FlatSeek: LLM-Driven Symbolic Discovery of Flat Outputs via Backward Data Generation
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: Differential flatness enables efficient planning and control, but discovering explicit flat outputs for general nonlinear systems remains difficult due to the lack of general methods and supervised data. We propose FlatSeek, a framework combining backward data generation with task-specific large language model (LLM) training. By reversing the defining reconstruction of flatness, we generate system-flat-output pairs with known certificates, then fine-tune an LLM to propose symbolic flat-output candidates for unseen dynamics. On literature and synthetic benchmarks, FlatSeek outperforms both the traditional symbolic methods and the untuned reference models in flat-output discovery success, and uncovers alternative symbolic flat outputs not reported in the literature.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Structure-Preserving Learning for Nonlinear Nonholonomic Dynamics
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: Learning the dynamics of mechanical systems subject to nonlinear nonholonomic constraints is challenging, as data-driven models may violate the underlying physical constraints, leading to inconsistent predictions. To address this problem, we develop a constraint-preserving learning framework based on the Lagrange-d'Alembert-Chetaev equations and tangency to the constraint submanifold, which together define an affine space of admissible accelerations. Using the kinetic-energy metric and the Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse, we construct a metric projector and the corresponding Chetaev correction. Embedding this geometric structure directly into a Gaussian process prior ensures that both prior and posterior dynamics satisfy the acceleration constraints exactly. We characterize the resulting reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS), derive an adapted-coordinate representation, and establish nonexpansiveness and consistency transfer. Numerical experiments on a three-dimensional directional flocking system with up to 50 agents demonstrate exact constraint preservation and robustness to constraint-incompatible observations.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Velocity-Free Funnel Control of Euler-Lagrange Systems: An Artificial-Delay Approach
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: Classical funnel control keeps the tracking error within a prescribed, time-varying envelope by increasing the feedback gain as the error approaches the boundary. For mechanical systems, this guarantee typically relies on velocity measurements. We show that it can be retained for fully actuated Euler--Lagrange systems using only position measurements. The proposed controller replaces the velocity error with a difference quotient of the position error over a fixed delay, while preserving the classical unbounded gain. It requires no plant model, reference derivatives, observer, or filter states. The central challenge is to reconcile the averaging inherent in delayed feedback with a gain that can grow without bound near the funnel boundary. We resolve this by establishing an a priori bound on the gain along closed-loop trajectories, independent of the delay. This bound yields a computable delay threshold that guarantees tracking within the prescribed funnel and boundedness of all closed-loop signals. The threshold depends only on bounds on the inertia, forces, and reference. Simulations demonstrate tracking accuracy comparable to full-state funnel control and tolerance of delays substantially longer than certified. With quantized position measurements, the controller also requires substantially less torque than an existing derivative-free funnel controller.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Energy system device sizing under closed-loop operation with imperfect forecasts
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: The value of renewable energy devices depends on their operation, which must adapt to weather and demand using limited, imperfect forecasts that update over time. Conventional energy systems planning practices assume unlimited foresight in a single-level formulation, potentially leading to long-term investment in suboptimal device sizes. Accounting for realistic operation corresponds to a bi-level problem: the upper level selects device sizes, while the lower level contains closed-loop operation under evolving forecasts. We solve this problem using backpropagation MPC (BP-MPC), a gradient-based method, with a deterministic MPC as the lower-level controller. Using forecast errors generated by a parameterized martingale model of forecast evolution, we investigate how forecast accuracy affects the benefits of operation-aware energy systems planning and the resulting device sizes. In a case study of an energy system comprising photovoltaics, a battery, a heat pump, and thermal storage with uncertain weather and energy demands, accounting for closed-loop operation yields higher average cost savings as forecast error increases. The resulting designs achieve these savings by progressively shifting investment from battery storage to solar generation and thermal storage, which buffers forecast mismatches.
Systems and Control (EESS).comment: 8 pages, 7 figures, 2 tables. Submitted to the 2027 European Control Conference (ECC)

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Ramping Procurement and Bid-Cost Recovery in Real-Time Market
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: We study ramping procurement co-optimized with economic dispatch under net-demand uncertainty. We examine two flexible ramp product designs implemented by grid operators: single-interval and multi-interval co-optimization. Both rely on rolling-window stochastic optimization with binding and advisory interval decisions. We develop analytical frameworks to evaluate generator profits, consumer payments, bid cost recovery (BCR), and operational efficiency. In particular, net-demand uncertainty may lead to generator under-compensation, requiring discriminatory BCR. While operational efficiency is invariant to energy and ramp prices, producer profits and consumer payments depend critically on pricing. We examine locational marginal pricing (LMP) and two uniform pricing: maximum dispatch cost pricing (MDCP) and maximum temporal locational marginal pricing (MTLMP). With out-of-market BCR, LMP yields discriminatory energy prices, whereas MDCP eliminates BCR and MTLMP does so in most cases. This property enables us to establish truthful bidding incentives for price-taking generators under MDCP. Our analysis highlights trade-offs between single- and multi-interval co-optimization and pricing designs: multi-interval energy-ramp co-optimization outperforms single-interval co-optimization when ramping forecasts are accurate and ramping needs are tight, but its advantage diminishes under large forecast errors and moderate ramping needs. Empirical results on CAISO and ERCOT data show that MDCP and MTLMP increase producer profits with negligible BCR, albeit at the expense of higher consumer payments relative to LMP.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Can STATCOM and UPS-Based Voltage Support Mitigate Fault-Induced Reductions in AI Data Center Grid Power Draw?
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: Artificial intelligence data centers (AIDCs) are rapidly increasing in number and capacity. These large electronic loads are interfaced through power electronic devices and can sharply reduce grid power intake during fault-induced voltage sags. Disturbances exceeding equipment ride-through capabilities may also trigger protective disconnection, posing risks to power system security. Static synchronous compensators (STATCOMs) and appropriately controlled AIDC uninterruptible power supply (UPS) rectifiers can provide reactive power support during voltage sags. This paper compares the individual and combined effectiveness of STATCOM and UPS-based voltage support in mitigating fault-induced reductions in grid power intake through electromagnetic transient simulations of a 1 GW AIDC connected to an IEEE nine-bus system. Simulation results show that STATCOM support better preserves short-term intake in milder tested faults, whereas UPS coordination maintains rectifier operation under deeper sags by reducing active intake to reserve reactive current capacity. Combined support improves auxiliary load retention and recovery in selected cases. However, severe tested sags still cause substantial grid-demand reductions even with combined support.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Incremental Model Predictive Control for Reference Tracking of Nonlinear Anesthesia Dynamics
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: Anesthesia dynamics are commonly described by Wiener models, consisting of linear dynamics followed by a static nonlinearity. This nonlinear output complicates the derivation of theoretical guarantees on closed-loop stability and convergence. Model Predictive Control (MPC) is particularly suitable for anesthesia control, as it explicitly accounts for constraints in the control design. In this paper, we propose an incremental MPC formulation for tracking a desired reference. The proposed approach exploits the structure of the nonlinear output equation to reformulate the control problem within a linear framework. An incremental model is then employed to avoid the explicit computation of steady states and inputs, which may be inaccurate in the presence of model uncertainties. The proposed controller is evaluated through simulations involving 1000 virtual patients and compared with a benchmark MPC formulation. Results show improved steady-state reference tracking while maintaining satisfactory disturbance rejection.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: A Joint LLM and Optimization Agent Solution for Drone Scheduling in Victim Search Missions
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: Victim search in wilderness areas is time-critical. Drones enable rapid area search, but scheduling them is challenging because victims may continue moving, detection results are uncertain, and effective decisions must combine structured mission information with unstructured contextual clues and domain knowledge. To address this, we propose an agent-aided drone scheduling system. The system employs an agent at the ground control station (GCS) to coordinate multiple drones over successive search cycles. In each cycle, the agent applies a scheduling policy that combines a large language model (LLM) for reasoning about where to search with an optimizer for determining how to dispatch the drones under energy constraints. Simulation results show that the proposed system consistently completes the victim-search mission, whereas none of the six non-LLM baselines does so and direct LLM scheduling is considerably less reliable. The source code is publicly available at https://github.com/1643204431/llm-uav-victim-search.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Input-output characterization of robotic grasping: Connecting design parameters to grasp behavior through the admittance
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: Low-impedance grippers make the dynamics of a grasp matter. Current grasp metrics, however, are static: they describe how a held object resists constant loads, not how it responds to time-varying ones. To quantify this, we rely on small-signal analysis to characterize a grasp by its admittance, the transfer matrix relating load perturbations to object displacements around an equilibrium. This transfer matrix recovers the stiffness and stability of the grasp at zero frequency and captures its natural frequencies and peak gain under time-varying loads. We apply this characterization to a planar two-finger gripper under proportional-derivative control. We show that two grasps of the same object in the same position and with the same contact forces can differ in stiffness by two orders of magnitude. Likewise, two grasps that share the same stiffness can exhibit very different resonances. Nonlinear simulations confirm the effectiveness of our small-signal analysis in capturing the dynamic behavior of grasping.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Mean--Variance Portfolio Selection by Continuous-Time Reinforcement Learning: Algorithms, Regret Analysis, and Empirical Study
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: We study continuous-time mean--variance portfolio selection in markets where stock prices are diffusion processes driven by observable factors that are also diffusion processes, yet the coefficients of these processes are unknown. Based on the recently developed reinforcement learning (RL) theory for diffusion processes, we present a general data-driven RL approach that learns the pre-committed investment strategy directly without attempting to learn or estimate the market coefficients. For multi-stock Black--Scholes markets without factors, we further devise an algorithm and prove its performance guarantee by deriving a sublinear regret bound in terms of the Sharpe ratio. We then carry out an extensive empirical study implementing this algorithm to compare its performance and trading characteristics, evaluated under a host of common metrics, with a large number of widely employed portfolio allocation strategies on S\&P 500 constituents. The results demonstrate that the proposed continuous-time RL strategy is consistently among the best, especially in a volatile bear market, and decisively outperforms the model-based continuous-time counterparts by significant margins.
Systems and Control (EESS).comment: 99 pages, includes appendix. Accepted for publication in Management Science

Systems and Control (EESS).title: ART for Diffusion Sampling: A Reinforcement Learning Approach to Timestep Scheduling
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: We consider time discretization for score-based diffusion models to generate samples from a learned reverse-time dynamic on a finite grid. Uniform and hand-crafted grids can be suboptimal given a budget on the number of time steps. We introduce Adaptive Reparameterized Time (ART), which controls the clock speed of a reparameterized time variable to redistribute computation along the sampling trajectory while preserving the terminal time, with the objective of minimizing the aggregate Euler discretization error. We derive a randomized companion ART-RL that recasts ART as a continuous-time reinforcement learning problem with Gaussian policies, and prove a two-directional bridge between the two: the deterministic ART optimum lifts to an optimal Gaussian policy, and conversely any optimal Gaussian policy must recover the ART control through its mean. This bridge turns continuous-time actor--critic learning into a principled, rather than heuristic, route to the deterministic timestep optimum. Within the official EDM pipeline, ART-RL improves FID on CIFAR--10 across a wide range of budgets; after one-time offline training, the distilled deterministic schedule transfers without retraining to AFHQv2, FFHQ, and ImageNet at no extra inference cost.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: On Energy-Based Modelling for Fluidic Excitable Neurons
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: Motivated by the potential of pneumatic excitable devices in soft robotics, this paper develops an energy-based, domain-agnostic equivalent of the Hodgkin-Huxley modelling framework using bond graph theory. The proposed model is used to guide the design of a pneumatic excitable neuron. The potential of this approach is illustrated through the design of a pneumatic half-center oscillator, an essential building block for rhythmic neuromorphic behaviours.
Systems and Control (EESS).comment: 6 pages, 5 figures, submitted to European Control Conference 2027

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Strategically Robust Multi-Agent Control
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: A key source of uncertainty in multi-agent systems is the behavior of other agents. Game-theoretic control approaches ignore this uncertainty, while robust control approaches treat others as fully adversarial. In this paper, we introduce strategically robust multi-agent control to populate the spectrum between these two paradigms. Specifically, in dynamic games, we propose that players are strategically robust and seek protection against misspecified control policies of the other players. This formulation induces a novel equilibrium concept, strategically robust dynamic equilibrium, that interpolates between game-theoretic control and robust control. We study this concept across canonical open- and closed-loop settings and show that accounting for strategic robustness also has computational benefits over classic approaches in game-theoretic control. Numerical experiments on vehicle platooning, inventory management, and network control illustrate resilience to misspecification, and also exhibit a "free-lunch" phenomenon in which strategic robustness can improve performance or social welfare.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Vector-Field-Guided Constraint-Following Control for Geometric Path Following of Uncertain Mechanical Systems
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: Achieving dynamics-level control is a critical yet challenging problem for accurate, high-speed geometric path-following of uncertain robotic systems. This paper proposes a vector-field-guided constraint-following control framework for geometric path following of uncertain mechanical systems. The key idea is to encode vector-field guidance as a velocity constraint, enabling a unified force/torque control design for a class of fully actuated and underactuated systems with desired paths that may be self-intersecting. A global, explicit error estimate connects constraint-following accuracy to path-following performance with convergence guarantees. An adaptive robust extension further addresses heterogeneous time-varying uncertainties with unknown bounds and ensures ultimately bounded path-following error. Applications to an underactuated aircraft system and a fully actuated manipulator system demonstrate the effectiveness and advantages of the framework.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Joint Communication-Control Strategy Optimization with Partially Nested Information Structures: The Linear-Quadratic Case
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: In this paper, we formalize a joint communication-control strategy optimization (JCCO) problem in multi-agent linear systems with quadratic costs, under the common-information-based (CIB) framework from decentralized stochastic control. For computational tractability, we focus on such JCCO problems with partially nested (PN) information structures (ISs). In particular, with a baseline communication protocol that leads to a PN IS, we establish a series of conditions under which the partial nestedness is preserved under the (additional) communication strategies to be optimized, while violating them may cause nonlinearity or non-existence of the optimal control strategies, with open-loop communication strategies. Under these conditions, we then develop a dynamic-programming-based approach to compute the optimal control strategies of JCCO with open-loop communication strategies, which yields a set of closed-form Riccati Equations. As a byproduct of independent interest, such an approach also offers a new way to solve decentralized linear-quadratic control with PN ISs and output feedback, under the CIB framework and the aforementioned conditions. Finally, we extend such an approach to JCCOs with closed-loop communication strategies, yielding a more tractable dynamic program than an infinite-dimensional CIB-belief-based one.
Systems and Control (EESS).comment: Preliminary version accepted to IEEE CDC 2026; Sharpened the proof of Lemma IV.5

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Semantic-Coupled Perception Framework for Autonomous Laparoscope Control
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: In minimally invasive surgery (MIS), maintaining an appropriate field of view (FoV) is essential for surgical safety and efficiency. However, conventional autonomous laparoscope control methods often treat visual tracking and surgical phase recognition independently, limiting robustness under occlusion, entity overlap, and camera motion. This paper proposes a closed-loop autonomous laparoscope control framework that couples real-time surgical phase recognition with camera-motion-compensated visual perception. By exploiting phase-dependent relationships among surgical entities, the framework improves target state estimation under challenging visual conditions, supporting task-aware autonomous FoV control. Benchmark and phantom experiments evaluate the framework in surgical phase recognition, target tracking under occlusion and entity overlap, and autonomous FoV control, showing improved target visibility and task execution compared with fixed-FoV control. These results highlight the potential of incorporating task-level semantics into visual state estimation for autonomous laparoscope guidance.
Systems and Control (EESS).comment: 8 pages, 5 figures. Submitted to IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters (RA-L) for possible publication

Systems and Control (EESS).title: DER Aggregators in Wholesale Electricity Markets: A Hybrid Mean-Field Framework with Endogenous Price Feedback
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: The rapid growth of distributed energy resources (DERs), including rooftop solar and energy storage, is transforming the grid edge, where customer-side assets increasingly interact with the broader power grid. DER aggregators, entities that coordinate the actions of many small-scale DERs, play a key role in this transformation. This paper presents a hybrid Mean-Field Control (MFC) and Mean-Field Game (MFG) framework for integrating DER aggregators into wholesale electricity markets. Unlike traditional approaches that treat market prices as exogenous, our model captures the feedback between aggregators' collective actions and electricity prices. The MFC component optimizes DER operations within each aggregator, while the MFG models strategic interactions among multiple aggregators. To account for various uncertainties, we incorporate reinforcement learning, which allows aggregators to learn optimal bidding strategies in dynamic market conditions. We prove the existence and uniqueness of a mean-field equilibrium and validate the framework through a case study of the Oahu Island power system. Results show that our approach reduces price volatility and improves market efficiency, offering a scalable and decentralized solution for DER integration in wholesale markets.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: GridForge: A Tractable Network-Flow Method for Constructing Open, Continental-Scale Synthetic Power Grids
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: The goal of this paper is to construct open, continental-scale synthetic transmission grids with an optimization method that stays tractable. Security restrictions keep models of the real grid out of open research and machine-learning datasets, and optimization-based construction is hard at scale: the number of candidate lines grows combinatorially, so electrically faithful methods prune the candidates in advance. This paper presents GridForge, which keeps every bus pair within physical length limits as a candidate, selects lines with Garver's length-weighted network-flow linear program instead of binary decisions, and resizes them with a sequential direct-current (DC) power flow. Two stages of 13 regional networks are evaluated. Their node-degree distributions are nearly as strongly log-linear as those of the real Eastern and Western Interconnections ($R^2$ of 0.92 to 0.98 against 0.971 and 0.981), although the areas under the fitted lines differ from the real ones by 39.9% on average. On the upper Midwest and Tennessee Valley footprints, resizing lowers the DC power-flow loss from 5.89% to 4.14% and from 14.55% to 7.05%, and the DC optimal power-flow loss from 4.03% to 2.02% and from 5.54% to 2.47%. Without relaxing any line limit, the DC optimal power flow is feasible in 78.81% and 0.82% of the scenarios. Most lines are built at 69 kV. The models span 250 to 78,484 buses, were built on single machines, and are freely redistributable.
Systems and Control (EESS).comment: 30 pages, 10 figures, 7 tables; supplementary material as an ancillary file. Submitted to the International Journal of Electrical Power & Energy Systems. Data: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24096575; code: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23826484

Systems and Control (EESS).title: A Coupled Control Barrier Function Approach to Deadlock-Free Multi-Robot Conflict Resolution
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: Many robotic applications involve scenarios where multiple robots interact and the decisions of one robot influence the behavior of others. This paper presents a quadratic programming (QP)-based feedback controller for multi-robot conflict resolution with input constraints. Safety is enforced using coupled Control Barrier Function (CBF), while a yielding matrix encodes how robots influence each other. Unlike existing methods with fixed or hard priorities, the proposed framework enables yielding preferences while guaranteeing deadlock-free operation by design. Sufficient conditions are established for the controller to be locally Lipschitz. The optimal CBF sign- indefinite slack is shown to admit a finite uniform bound, which is compensated through an enlarged CBF safety margin to obtain a forward invariant set contained within the desired safe set. The analysis also identifies an irreducible slack component due to finite maximum deceleration that cannot be eliminated by increasing the slack penalty. Finally, sufficient conditions on the yielding matrix and nominal controller are derived to exclude deadlock states. Simulations demonstrate adaptive coordination across yielding preferences and robustness to robot failures.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Physics-informed Learning for Orbital Uncertainty Propagation with Error Bounds
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: The Fokker-Planck partial differential equation (FP-PDE) governs uncertainty evolution in stochastic dynamical systems. In orbital dynamics, solving the FP-PDE is challenging because of nonlinear motion, high-dimensional states, and large space-time domains. We develop a physics-informed neural network (PINN) approach that approximates the FP-PDE solution as a single space-time probability density, while also quantifying its worst-case approximation error. This approach is, in principle, independent of the choice of state coordinates and neural network architecture. Specifically, to enforce probability density function (PDF) properties into the neural network, we design a Physics-informed Gaussian mixture model (PINN-GMM). Then a companion error PINN learns the dynamics of the approximation error and yields time-dependent bounds that define an ambiguity set of PDFs. This ambiguity set enables rigorous computation of upper and lower bounds on event probabilities through tractable linear programs. Numerical studies on illustrative 1D examples and several 4D--6D orbital test cases demonstrate accurate uncertainty propagation, correct and informative error bounds, and improved reliability over common uncertainty-propagation baseline methods (Gaussian approximation, unscented transform, and Gaussian mixture model). Constructing the PINN-GMM requires offline training, making it costlier than the baseline approximations; once trained, however, a single forward pass returns the density at any time in sub-millisecond time $(0.16~\mathrm{ms}$ in our implementation).
Systems and Control (EESS).comment: Accepted to Journal of Guidance, Control, and Dynamics

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Fair and Efficient Distributed EV Charging Coordination Using Threshold Cryptography and Machine Learning
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: Distributed coordination of electric vehicle (EV) charging with the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) keeps EV constraints private but assumes that every participant follows the algorithm. This assumption fails in practice, where a biased operator or a man-in-the-middle (MITM) attacker can send inconsistent signals to different EVs, and compromised EVs can deviate from their prescribed updates. We first prove that attacks by such arbitrarily malicious, i.e., Byzantine, participants do not prevent convergence and therefore remain undetected, and derive the most damaging attack in closed form. We then propose a framework that combines a threshold-signed broadcast with upload recomputation, which detects every deviation without false alarms at linear instead of quadratic communication cost. To keep the optimization running, each affected EV recovers locally with a certified, fleet-aware machine learning price forecast, and we prove that the optimization remains convergent with a recovery cost bounded by the shape of the forecast error. Simulation results with real-world load, price, and charging data show that a biased operator raises the annual cost of disadvantaged EVs by 132.7% and lowers that of advantaged EVs by 49.3% without changing the aggregate load, whereas the defense limits all cost changes to 2.6%. An external MITM attacker raises the cost of its victims by 57.6%, the peak load by 5.8%, and the grid cost by 15.8%, whereas the defense keeps them within 1.1%, 0.2%, and 0.3% of benign operation. With up to 70% of the EVs attacked, the recovery converges in at least 97.8% of the runs.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Natural Swing-Up of an Underpowered Double Pendulum
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: Robots with weak motors must ride their natural dynamics rather than fight them. We swing up a direct-drive planar two-link robot, whose motors deliver only about 6\,\% of its shoulder gravity torque, along its nonlinear normal modes, two-dimensional invariant manifolds consisting of periodic orbits. On a non-strict mode, injecting energy necessarily moves the state off the manifold, so pumping and stabilization compete for the same bounded torque. We split the input torque into a power-neutral steering component and a scalar pumping input, the only component that changes the energy. The allocation then becomes a linear program in two variables: maximize pumping subject to the torque limits and one control-Lyapunov constraint. The constraint uses the model-based rate of the error, so no stabilizing feedback gain is needed. Experiments in hardware show swing-ups along both modes and compare the allocation with summing-and-clipping and with prioritized stabilization.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Symbolic Control for Stochastic Systems via Finite Parity Games
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: We consider the problem of computing the maximal probability of satisfying an omega-regular specification for stochastic nonlinear systems evolving in discrete time. The problem reduces, after automata-theoretic constructions, to finding the maximal probability of satisfying a parity condition on a (possibly hybrid) state space. While characterizing the exact satisfaction probability is open, we show that a lower bound on this probability can be obtained by (I) computing an under-approximation of the qualitative winning region, i.e., states from which the parity condition can be enforced almost surely, and (II) computing the maximal probability of reaching this qualitative winning region. The heart of our approach is a technique to symbolically compute the under-approximation of the qualitative winning region in step (I) via a finite-state abstraction of the original system as a 2.5-player parity game. Our abstraction procedure uses only the support of the probabilistic evolution; it does not use precise numerical transition probabilities. We prove that the winning set in the abstract 2.5-player game induces an under-approximation of the qualitative winning region in the original synthesis problem, along with a policy to solve it. By combining these contributions with (a) a symbolic fixpoint algorithm to solve 2.5-player games and (b) existing techniques for reachability policy synthesis in stochastic nonlinear systems, we get an abstraction-based algorithm for finding a lower bound on the maximal satisfaction probability. We have implemented the abstraction-based algorithm in Mascot-SDS (Majumdar et al., 2020), where we combined the outlined abstraction step with our recent tool FairSyn. We evaluated our implementation on the nonlinear model of a perturbed bistable switch from the literature. We outperform a recently proposed tool for solving this problem by a large margin.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Sub-Synchronous Control Interaction Risk of Large Data Center Loads: A Frequency-Scan Assessment with Cross-Model Validation
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: Data centers are now one of the fastest-growing loads on the bulk power system, and most of their demand reaches the grid through power converters inside uninterruptible power supplies (UPS). Whether these loads can take part in sub-synchronous control interaction (SSCI), as wind and HVDC converters do, has not been studied extensively. We examine this question with impedance-based frequency scans at the point of common coupling (PCC). Using a detailed proprietary model (INS-ISU), we scan the motor, variable-frequency-drive (VFD), lighting, and UPS-fed information-technology (IT) branches of a representative facility separately. Only the UPS in double-conversion mode shows negative resistance; it covers the whole sub-synchronous band and continues up to about 170 Hz. The other branches, and the UPS in bypass mode, stay passive. We then repeat the scans on three public models from PNNL, TAMU, and NLR. None of them shows negative resistance in bypass mode, while three of the four models do in double-conversion mode. Lowering the load from rated to light load makes the negative resistance deeper, as expected for a constant-power load, so a lightly loaded facility in double-conversion mode is the worst case. Raising the UPS DC-link capacitance pushes the negative resistance into a narrow band around the fundamental. These findings give a basis for screening data centers for SSCI during interconnection studies.
Systems and Control (EESS).comment: 13 pages, 16 figures. Submitted for IEEE publications

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Learning monotone game-theoretic linear MPC
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: We propose a method to learn a game-theoretic model predictive control (GT-MPC) law by imitation from input and output data of a running multi-agent system. By interpreting the recorded inputs as the first moves of the equilibria of a game played by the agents, we learn the GT-MPC weights under hard input constraints and soft output constraints, without requiring the agents to reveal their objectives. We also impose that the resulting generalized Nash equilibrium (GNE) problem is strongly monotone, which ensures the existence and uniqueness of the equilibrium and, hence, that the learned GT-MPC law is well defined and can be evaluated efficiently online by variational GNE-seeking algorithms for linear-quadratic games. Moreover, strong monotonicity implies that the equilibrium is almost everywhere differentiable with respect to the references and the weights, which enables automatic differentiation for gradient-based optimization. In addition, we promote closed-loop stability of the unconstrained equilibrium feedback by incorporating a penalty that involves a jointly learned quadratic Lyapunov function. Learning a GT-MPC formulation enables us to explain the agents' objectives, reproduce their behavior in simulation in new scenarios, optimize their set-points, design mechanisms, and enforce additional constraints. A numerical example illustrates the approach.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: RAZeR: Representation Aware Zonotope Reduction
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: Reachability analysis is a popular technique for verifying the safety of a dynamical system under uncertainty, where the uncertainty is often represented by zonotopes. As the size of the zonotope representation typically grows as the reachability analysis progresses, it must be repeatedly reduced at the cost of additional conservatism. While various methods exist to reduce the size of the representation, combined advantages are not fully leveraged as only a single reduction method is typically used throughout the analysis. In this work, we show how dynamically choosing which method to use can yield significantly tighter results, thereby easing verification. This is realized by introducing a heuristic, derived from model predictive control, that accounts for upcoming propagation of the current zonotope. We argue that order reduction is not merely a post-processing step after propagation but also a pre-processing step that shapes how the zonotope evolves under the system dynamics. We evaluate our approach, RAZeR, on nonlinear benchmarks taken from the ARCH-COMP, where we demonstrate that RAZeR produces tighter zonotopes at a negligible performance overhead.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Expert-Guided Online Reinforcement Learning for Stable and Sample-Efficient Control of Dynamical Systems
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: Online reinforcement learning (RL) often requires extensive interactions with the environment, which makes the training costly. Additionally, exploration can destabilise the dynamical system, which may be unsafe. On the other hand, offline learning from expert demonstrations avoids unsafe exploration but is limited by the quality and coverage of the offline dataset. In this paper, we propose a model-free RL approach that combines expert demonstrations with limited online interactions. Specifically, we optimise a policy objective consisting of an online performance term and a behavioural cloning regulariser computed from offline expert demonstrations. The regulariser encourages the learned policy to stay close to expert behaviour, reducing the need to explore unfamiliar actions. Expert demonstrations guide policy learning and reduce the need for many online interactions and exploration. For stochastic linear time-invariant (LTI) systems, we establish conditions for linear convergence of exact policy gradient updates and for all intermediate policies to remain stabilising. Although our theoretical analysis focuses on linear systems, we also evaluate the proposed approach on nonlinear systems to demonstrate its effectiveness beyond the linear setting. \rev{Numerical results show that the proposed method reaches comparable performance in fewer gradient steps and with less number of samples than a purely online RL baseline.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Methanol substitution suppresses deflagration-excited knock and increases the efficiency of a hydrogen-fuelled CFR engine
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: Knock restricts the performance of hydrogen spark-ignition engines and is usually attributed to end-gas autoignition. To the authors' knowledge, this is the first study in which methanol is used to replace part of the hydrogen in a hydrogen engine at constant fuel energy addition, and it shows that near the knock boundary the limiting oscillation is excited by the deflagration itself, which methanol removes without derating the performance. Port-injected methanol replaced 20--50% of the hydrogen energy in a variable-compression Cooperative Fuel Research engine at 600 rpm and compression ratios of 8--12. With pure hydrogen, oscillation in the 4--15 kHz range began before 10% of the charge had burned in 97--100% of cycles, and its maximum amplitude (MAPO) followed the maximum pressure-rise rate across 2499 cycles (Spearman $ρ=0.94$). Methanol slowed the deflagration: it replaced high-flame-speed hydrogen, cooled the intake by 24--25 K and, at unchanged intake pressure, enleaned the mixture by 10--13%. At 50% methanol, the 10--90% combustion duration lengthened 2.7--3.0-fold, oscillation onset moved 4.5--8.3$^\circ$CA after CA10 and mean MAPO fell by 89--93% although the spark timing was advanced by 13--19$^\circ$CA, and IMEP and indicated thermal efficiency rose by 2.4--7.8%. Methanol was thus worth more than this advance, and at matched CA50 MAPO was still about 90% lower. The measured combustion duration of all 25 data sets scaled with the computed laminar flame speed as $S_L^{-0.58}$ ($R^2=0.99$); fuel replacement accounted for about three quarters of the reduction in $S_L$, and the end-gas autoignition integral stayed below 0.07, against 1 at autoignition. The chamber kept its cylindrical acoustic modes, whose frequencies fell by 8--9%. The trade-off is formaldehyde emissions, which rose five- to sixfold while NO$_x$ fell by 49--85%.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Admissibility-Preserving Control for Block Strict-Feedback Systems Under Time-Varying Asymmetric Actuator and State Constraints
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: This paper addresses the tracking control of block strict-feedback nonlinear systems subject to time-varying asymmetric actuator and full state constraints. To that end, we develop a time-varying Admissibility-Preserving Control (APC) framework, in which the Admissibility-Preserving Input Realization (APIR) generates the plant input through a dynamic realization. The APIR guarantees input admissibility under the moving actuator set whenever each actuator bound contracts slower than the decay rate of the realization, and a closed-form lower bound on its gain is derived. The state constraints are handled by a logarithmic barrier coordinate at every backstepping step, with widths measured from the virtual control to the moving envelope of the corresponding state. We prove that every state lies inside its envelope, with each virtual control only required to remain inside the envelope of the next state, while the tracking error converges to zero exponentially. Simulations demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed safety-critical control scheme.

Robotics.title: COSMO-Bench: A Benchmark for Collaborative SLAM Optimization
Robotics.summary: Recent years have seen a focus on research into distributed optimization algorithms for multi-robot Collaborative Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (C-SLAM). Research in this domain, however, is made difficult by a lack of standard benchmark datasets. Such datasets have been used to great effect in the field of single-robot SLAM, and researchers focused on multi-robot problems would benefit greatly from dedicated benchmark datasets. To address this gap, we design and release the Collaborative Open-Source Multi-robot Optimization Benchmark (COSMO-Bench) -- a suite of 24 datasets derived from a baseline C-SLAM front-end and real-world LiDAR data. Data DOI: https://doi.org/10.1184/R1/29652158
Robotics.comment: This article has been accepted for publication in IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation. DOI: 10.1109/ICRA57385.2026.11696499

Robotics.title: Robo-SWE: An Executable Issue-Resolution Dataset Mined from Robot Software Repositories
Robotics.summary: Coding agents are evaluated mostly on general-purpose software, but domain-specific systems require domain-aware evaluation. Robot software is a particularly challenging case: Robot Operating System 2 (ROS 2) packages have their own build tools, simulators and learning frameworks are built on physics engines, and behavior that depends on timing and hardware is hard to test. We present Robo-SWE, a dataset of 236 executable issue-resolution tasks mined from merged pull requests in 28 public robotics repositories in four domains: ROS 2 systems, simulation and physics engines, robotics algorithm libraries, and robot-learning frameworks. Each task contains the original issue text, a container recipe for the repository at the commit before the fix, the developers' fix, and the developers' tests, which fail before the fix and pass after it in repeated offline runs. The dataset also keeps a provenance ledger of all 1,567 candidate pull requests, with the stage each reached and the reason for every rejection, and, as a first use, 3,540 graded attempts by five coding-agent setups with recorded patches and 3,529 available trajectories. Across three runs per primary setup, resolve rates range from 45.8% for Claude Sonnet 5.5 to 56.5% for Claude Opus 5.5; GPT-6.1 Sol reaches 54.1% at maximum effort and 52.5% at medium effort, and GPT-6 Astra 51.4%. GLM-5.3 resolves 46.2%, and Kimi K3.1 Pro 43.9%. The tasks are validated by execution; verification of their fairness by human reviewers is future work. The dataset and public leaderboard are available online.
Robotics.comment: 5 pages, 1 figure, 2 tables. Submitted to the MSR 2027 Data and Tool Showcase Track. Dataset: https://huggingface.co/datasets/vharatian/Robo-SWE

Robotics.title: riMESA: Consensus ADMM for Real-World Collaborative SLAM
Robotics.summary: Collaborative Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (C-SLAM) is a fundamental capability for multi-robot teams as it enables downstream tasks like planning and navigation. However, existing C-SLAM back-end algorithms that are required to solve this problem struggle to address the practical realities of real-world deployments (i.e. communication limitations, outlier measurements, and online operation). In this paper we propose Robust Incremental Manifold Edge-based Separable ADMM (riMESA) -- a robust, incremental, and distributed C-SLAM back-end that is resilient to outliers, reliable in the face of limited communication, and can compute accurate state estimates for a multi-robot team in real-time. Through the development of riMESA, we, more broadly, make an argument for the use of Consensus Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers as a theoretical foundation for distributed optimization tasks in robotics like C-SLAM due to its flexibility, accuracy, and fast convergence. We conclude this work with an in-depth evaluation of riMESA on a variety of C-SLAM problem scenarios and communication network conditions using both synthetic and real-world C-SLAM data. These experiments demonstrate that riMESA is able to generalize across conditions, produce accurate state estimates, operate in real-time, and outperform the accuracy of prior works by a factor >7x on real-world datasets.
Robotics.comment: This article has been accepted for publication in IEEE Transactions on Robotics. DOI: 10.1109/TRO.2026.3706569

Robotics.title: Dataset-Free Compliant Humanoid Loco-Manipulation with Dynamic Online Posture
Robotics.summary: Most humanoid loco-manipulation controllers require human motion data to learn whole-body coordination and posture, leaving policies reliant on external sources to provide this data. We present OCLO (Online-posture Compliant LOco-manipulation), a humanoid loco-manipulation system trained without human motion data and commanded only through two end-effector targets and a walking velocity. Because these targets do not uniquely determine whole-body posture, OCLO generates pelvis height and torso orientation online using an analytic reachability prior, further refined through policy-in-the-loop sampling with a task-agnostic cost. OCLO also learns whole-body compliance by displacing end-effector references according to measured forces through a spring-damper model, encouraging the legs, waist, and pelvis to yield to external loads. In simulation, using the reachability prior leads to a 77.8% success rate in acquiring the commanded reference, a vast improvement over the 37.8% success rate accomplished without the prior. Further, refinement reduces end-effector orientation error across all evaluated tasks. The same posture module improves a pretrained SONIC controller on all five tasks. Without compliance training, policies tend to lose balance under disturbances rather than sacrifice tracking. On a Unitree G1, OCLO maintains balance under end-effector disturbances that cause its ablations to fail and performs nine loco-manipulation tasks, including crouched walking and picking up a box from a low surface. Project website: https://oclo-humanoid.github.io/

Robotics.title: AVI-HT: Adaptive Vision-IMU Fusion for 3D Gloved Hand Tracking
Robotics.summary: We present AVI-HT, an adaptive visual-IMU fusion approach for tracking 3D hand poses by jointly modeling the egocentric images with on-glove 6-DoF IMU signals. AVI-HT significantly improved accuracy and availability, particularly in hand-object interaction (HOI) scenarios involving heavy visual occlusion. Two complementary ingredients underpin its success: (1) synchronized multi-modal training data pairing on-body vision-IMU sensor streams with ground-truth 3D hand poses from a motion-capture system, and (2) a cross-sensor deep attention mechanism that adaptively modulates the trust assigned to the vision and individual IMU sensors. To evaluate AVI-HT in real-world settings, we conduct extensive experiments on our DexGloveHOI dataset that consists of 100K+ pairwise vision-IMU samples with synchronized 3D annotated poses, in which users manipulate a variety of objects during daily tasks. We compare against multiple single- and multi-modal tracking approaches under two hand models (UmeTrack, MANO). The results show that AVI-HT reduces mean keypoint error by 16.1% and its wrist-aligned variant by 24.2% over the baselines. A hand-object contact evaluation shows that AVI-HT keeps finger contacts with the manipulated object more accurately and consistently over time, reducing contact losses by 8.5%. Ablation studies further show that our fusion design outperforms simpler schemes and that the gains grow with occlusion and hold across subjects.

Robotics.title: QuantGraph: A Receding-Horizon Quantum Graph Solver
Robotics.summary: Dynamic programming is a cornerstone of graph-based optimization. While effective, it scales unfavorably with problem size. In this work, we present QuantGraph, a two-stage quantum-enhanced framework that casts local and global graph-optimization problems as quantum-searches over discrete trajectory spaces. The solver is designed to operate efficiently by first finding a sequence of locally optimal transitions in the graph (local stage), without considering full trajectories. The accumulated cost of the resulting candidate acts as a threshold that prunes the search space (up to 60% reduction for certain examples). The subsequent global stage, based on this threshold, refines the solution. To achieve scalability and robustness, we draw on principles from control theory and embed QuantGraph's global stage within a receding-horizon model-predictive-control scheme. This classical layer stabilizes and guides the quantum search, improving precision and reducing computational burden. In practice, the resulting closed-loop system exhibits robust behavior and lower query complexity. Notably, for a fixed control horizon and query budget, QuantGraph supports approximately twice as many control discretization bits while still benefiting from Grover-search's inherent quadratic speedup compared to classical methods.
Robotics.comment: P. Vaidhyanathan and A. Papatheodorou contributed equally to this work. Published in Physical Review Applied. 17 pages, 4 figures, 2 tables, 2 algorithms

Robotics.title: Imitating the Imperfect: Offline-to-Online Robust Imitation Learning from Heterogeneous Demonstrators
Robotics.summary: Imitation learning (IL) typically relies on large-scale offline demonstrations collected from multiple human or algorithmic demonstrators. However, most existing approaches assume these demonstrators are homogeneous or near-optimal experts, a convenient but unrealistic assumption in real-world applications. In practice, demonstrations are often collected from heterogeneous demonstrators with unknown and varying levels of expertise, resulting in highly mixed-quality data. In this work, we study a challenging yet practical setting of imitation learning from such heterogeneous imperfect demonstrators. We propose Latent Expertise and Optimality Scoring based Imitation Learning (LEOS-IL), a principled framework that jointly learns (i) a state-action optimality scoring model and (ii) latent expertise levels for each demonstrator from unlabeled suboptimal offline demonstrations. The learned scoring model is then integrated into an online policy optimization procedure, where the agent is trained to maximize estimated optimality scores while its online rollouts are iteratively leveraged to refine the scoring model, thereby mitigating distributional shift during online adaptation. We further provide theoretical guarantees for optimality score identification and conditional optimal occupancy and policy recovery under explicit sufficient conditions. Experiments on continuous control benchmarks demonstrate that our approach consistently outperforms existing baselines across highly heterogeneous and low-quality demonstration regimes.

Robotics.title: JustRUA: A Controlled Study of GPT-6 Robot-Use Agents
Robotics.summary: GPT-6 Astra can drive a robot arm directly through a fixed harness, and scores of such robot-use agents on RoboDojo have risen quickly since. Reported systems differ in harness and test subset and often change several designs at once, so it is hard to tell which choices produce the gains. We take these designs apart and test them in one framework, along the harness around the model, the action interface, the reuse of experience and the scene geometry given to the model. A lean harness that keeps the full episode history and stops each motion early goes a long way. Reusing experience changes how the model acts but is not a free lunch, and scene geometry helps most, even when depth is predicted from RGB alone. JustRUA starts from the official L3 harness and keeps only what matters most. Even with no learned policy, self-improvement loop or task-specific tuning, this simple harness raises the score on the RoboDojo simulation benchmark substantially, from 29.7 to 50.3.
Robotics.comment: 30 pages, 14 figures. Project page: https://zefanw.github.io/JustRUA. Code: https://github.com/ZefanW/JustRUA

Robotics.title: Discrete Model-Based Diffusion for Combinatorial Optimization in Multi-Robot Task Allocation
Robotics.summary: Decision making in multi-robot systems often involves discrete decision variables, leading to NP-hard combinatorial optimization problems that must be solved within seconds for near real-time implementation. Denoising diffusion has emerged as a powerful tool for such problems, but existing approaches face a trade-off: Model-Based Diffusion (MBD) incorporates diffusion in sampling-based optimization (SBO) without training but only over continuous spaces, while existing diffusion-based combinatorial solvers operate over discrete spaces but require offline training. To this end, we propose Discrete Model-Based Diffusion (Discrete MBD), a training-free SBO method that directly optimizes discrete variables by approximating categorical reverse transition distributions through Monte Carlo sampling. We establish a finite-step lower bound on the probability of finding a global minimizer and show that this bound converges to one as the number of denoising steps increases. Extensive experiments on generic integer programs and heterogeneous multi-robot coalition formation and scheduling demonstrate that Discrete MBD outperforms SBO baselines in nearly all settings while achieving solution quality competitive with that of mixed-integer programming and reinforcement learning methods at a fraction of their computational cost.

Robotics.title: DexRemo: A Force-Sensing Hand Platform and Task Suite for Contact-Rich Removal Manipulation
Robotics.summary: Many manipulation tasks require separating adhered, embedded, contaminated, or mechanically constrained targets. We study this setting as removal manipulation, where progress depends on evolving contact states that are only partially observable from vision and kinematics. We introduce DexRemo, a three-finger robotic hand with high-force actuation, modular fingertips, and three-axis fingertip force sensing, together with a nine-scenario real-robot task suite spanning adhesive detachment, surface cleaning and self-cleaning, and occluded retrieval. To make multi-finger force observations easier to fuse, we express fingertip forces in a shared wrist-centered frame, giving force components consistent geometric meaning across fingers and time. Using an Action Chunking Transformer backbone, policies fuse multi-view vision, proprioception, fingertip pose, and force observations to predict closed-loop action chunks from demonstrations. Evaluation uses six core benchmark tasks for controlled fingertip-input and force-frame ablations, plus three extension scenarios for additional held-out coverage. Across these evaluations, the learned policies achieve consistent removal performance, and ablations show that wrist-frame forces, especially with fingertip pose, improve stability and generalization over local-frame force inputs and no-force baselines. Project website: https://dexremo.github.io
Robotics.comment: Accepted for publication in IEEE Transactions on Robotics (T-RO), 2026. Project website: https://dexremo.github.io

Robotics.title: Video-Action Models for Data-Efficient Industrial Manipulation
Robotics.summary: Industrial manipulation requires precise alignment and controlled handling of rigid, deformable, and flexible components. Yet, the benefits of pretrained visuomotor policies remain underexplored in settings where limited access to specialized hardware, components, and fixtures constrains demonstration collection and evaluation. Understanding task-specific data requirements is important for assessing their scalability across diverse processes on the factory floor. We investigate whether video pretraining can support reliable industrial manipulation with limited action data. We propose FLUX-mimic, a video-action model, motivated by the potential of video pretraining to capture motion and interaction patterns that enable sample-efficient training. FLUX-mimic is built on a backbone pretrained on large-scale web and industrial task data, and an action expert to generate robot trajectories. We train our policy by joint video-action training. Across four automotive manufacturing benchmark tasks and two bimanual robot platforms, FLUX-mimic outperforms all considered baselines on the dexterous robot platform and matches pi_{0.5}'s average success rate on the gripper-based robot platform. On a deformable part kitting task, FLUX-mimic reaches 77.5% success with as little as two hours of task-specific action-labeled demonstrations.

Robotics.title: COMBS: Concealed Object Multi-modal Bayesian Search
Robotics.summary: This work addresses the problem of finding a concealed object in an environment by unifying formalisms for partially observable environments with multi-modal priors drawn from a mix of ontologies, semantic networks, LLMs, and VLMs. We propose a concealment-adaptive mixed-observability MDP (CA-MOMDP), a Bayes-adaptive setting where uncertainty is over both object locations and which nodes can conceal them, held as a hypothesis with a bounded ontology prior and resolved only by interaction. We define a hierarchical transition system (HTS) to abstract the environment into room and object nodes that can be planned over via our CA-MOMDP. We further propose a COMBS-score: a multi-modal fusion of a human informed semantic network, LLM, and VLM, to initialize the belief over object locations, which grounds our abstractions and reduces reliance on a single model. Belief is maintained via Bayes' rule, which never lets a look rule out a closed container. We prove a present target is found in a bounded number of searches under exact perception and that its location is never ruled out given missed detection under noisy perception. We ablate each component to demonstrate their significance. Across five simulator configurations, from a gridworld to Matterport3D with a real detector, COMBS finds 92-100% of in-distribution and 92-100% of out-of-distribution targets, matches or beats the baselines in processing speed, significantly outperforms a per-step LLM policy at lower cost on the larger scenes, recovers more out-of-distribution placements than a TidyBot ranking, and matches an LLM-only prior at a fraction of its per-decision latency. COMBS is the only standalone method that can declare a target absent at a stated error level, and the per-step LLM policy offered a termination action abandons 12-22% of targets that were present, against 1.6-3.2% for COMBS on the same episodes.

Robotics.title: BiGym 2.0: Benchmarking Learned and Agent-Developed Policies for Humanoid Household Manipulation
Robotics.summary: Humanoid household manipulation requires the arms to act while the body balances, steps and changes posture. We present BiGym 2.0, an adaptation of BiGym for the Unitree G1 across 20 household tasks using a unified whole-body controller for demonstration and evaluation. The suite provides 60 native human virtual-reality demonstrations per task with synchronised multi-camera views and full-body execution records. We benchmark vision-language-action fine-tuning, imitation learning, demo-driven reinforcement learning, and cold-start coding agents given the interaction budget of online reinforcement learning. With the same onboard views, proprioception and whole-body controller for every method, vision-language-action fine-tuning has the highest nine-task mean, and agent-developed programs outperform every demo-driven reinforcement learning baseline on this mean and lead on bimanual reaching. Cross-workspace stacking remains open, $π_{0.5}$ stays low on pick-box, and multi-object transport is hard for imitation learning, demo-driven reinforcement learning and coding agents. All environments, human demonstrations, and evaluation traces are open-sourced at https://github.com/swirl-uk/BiGym2.
Robotics.comment: 23 pages. v3: Fig. 2 shows the torso-pitch body command used on 14 tasks; gripper named Dex1-1 throughout; seed notation
